worst_places.after:
Call it before `consume`: it sets the channel's QoS (Quality of Service — how many messages the broker may keep in flight) before any messages start flowing. How to pick the value:

- `prefetch(1)` — strict fairness and ordering, but low throughput.
- `prefetch(10–50)` — the balanced choice for typical background jobs.
- `prefetch(100+)` — high throughput for fast, I/O-light consumers, at the cost of more memory.

A message queue breaks this coupling in three ways:

- **Temporal decoupling** — producer and consumer don't have to be available at the same time.

patterns: Abbreviations are expanded once per ZONE, not once per FILE, and the expansion always lives in the earliest article that mentions the term. AMQP is spelled out in 01 and 02 but bare in 03; TTL and DLQ are spelled out in 03 and then used bare in 04, 05, 06 and 07 — including in 04, whose whole subject is dead-lettering. 'Visibility timeout' and 'redrive policy' are explained only in 05 and used bare in 07. QoS, TPS, SNS, HA, SLA and FIFO are never expanded anywhere in the zone. Since files are read out of order, the deepest articles are the least self-contained.

Article 07 abandons the format that makes 01-06 work. Articles 01-06 back every new concept with a code block, an ASCII diagram or a bullet list within a paragraph or two. Article 07 is 2.2-2.6k words with zero diagrams and zero code blocks, and every enumeration that would be a bullet list in 01-06 is inlined as '(1) … (2) … (3) …' inside a single 45-64 word sentence. This is the zone's only self-test surface (no question bank, no quiz), so the format costs the most exactly where the reader is meant to be recalling rather than reading.

The English version is consistently harder than the Russian for the same content. Russian files have 0-1 sentences over the length threshold each; English files have 3-26 (07: 15.1% of all sentences). English also adds idiom the Russian renders plainly: 'this works fine until it doesn't', 'it falls over entirely', 'gets hammered with', 'the most important tuning knob', 'pays for itself', 'poison pill', 'the scaling story', 'blind-retry'. Three EN-only defects have no ru counterpart at all: the 'goroutines' leak (03), the broken quote markup (03), and the garbled saga diagram (06).

Russian keeps English terms as bare loanwords with no gloss on first use in the file: downstream, replay, retention, payload, backoff, upsert, rate limit, fan-out, eventual consistency, best practice, батчинг. Most are genuinely untranslatable in this domain, but the first occurrence in each file needs three words of Russian in brackets — the articles already do this well for offset, wire-level, wildcards and quorum queues, so the habit exists and is just applied unevenly.
